title: Fault
description: A named error. Faults are ELEMENT-FIRST — they hang off slots, not styles, because most builder-grade errors are universal: the half-width shutter is wrong on every house that has shutters. Style is a facet, carried in applies_to and, more importantly, in exceptions: the cases where a style legitimately does the thing that is a fault everywhere else. A Georgian entry portico is five feet deep, which is a fault by Craftsman rules and correct by its own. A corpus that cannot say that will make a traditional design system worse rather than better.

name.description: Short and memorable. This becomes the thing a builder and a client can both say out loud.

slots.description: Element slot ids this fault attaches to. The primary index.

severity.description: fatal: destroys the style reading, and no amount of quality elsewhere recovers it. serious: visibly wrong to anyone trained, and cheap to have avoided. minor: a refinement that separates good from very good.

frequency.description: How often it actually occurs in contemporary production building. Endemic faults are where the leverage is.

category.description: profile-depth covers the whole family of errors where the shape is right and the relief is too shallow to cast a shadow — arguably the single largest category in contemporary work.

symptom.description: What you actually see. Written so someone who is not an architect can check it.

cause.description: WHY it happens. Almost never ignorance — nearly always a stock size, a trade sequence, a code, or a line item. Naming the driver is what makes the fault fixable rather than merely deplorable.

cost_saved.description: Roughly what the shortcut saves, because the argument for doing it right has to survive contact with a budget.

cost_negative.description: True where the fault actually COSTS money rather than saving it — a picturesque parti on a formal style, or pitch drift between wings. It changes the argument entirely: nobody is defending a budget.

kind.description: Added `code` in 0.2.0 — three authors independently reached for it. A house can be code-minimum and wrong, and the code is a real authority a fault is traded against, not a first principle.

ref.description: pack id and target_slot, style id, or a stated principle

correct_practice.description: What to do instead, with numbers wherever numbers exist.

fixes.description: Three tiers, because budget is real and a corpus that only offers the expensive answer gets ignored. The cheap tier is the one that actually gets built.

cheap.description: The best available answer at no or low added cost. Often a change of proportion or placement rather than of material.

dishonest.description: The tempting shortcut that looks like a fix and is not. Naming it is protective.

detection.description: How to spot it fast, from the street or from a photograph. Written for both a person and a model looking at an image.

applies_to.description: Style node ids, or the single token 'universal' where the fault applies wherever the element occurs.

exceptions.description: Where this is NOT a fault. Some styles play with an element far more than others, and a corpus that flattens that will produce timid, generic buildings.

style.description: style node id, or a construction or region token

bounds.description: How far the licence extends, so an exception does not become a loophole.

bounds_test.description: The numeric form of `bounds`, so an exception can be checked rather than merely read. Without it an exception becomes a loophole.

granted_when.description: A precondition on the CONTEXT -- the wall, the roof, the site -- as `applies_to_styles` is a precondition on the style and `test.applies_when` is a precondition on the measurements. An exception often depends on construction or region, not only on style: the Shingle Style corner licence holds only where the cladding is actually shingle, and only where the corner is woven. RENAMED FROM `applies_when` ON 28 AUG 2026 (WP-8.4). This schema carried two fields of that name meaning different things -- one a precondition on measurements, evaluated since WP-5.13; this one a precondition on context, populated on 331 exceptions and evaluated by nothing at all for as long as it had existed. Two mechanisms under one name is the condition under which `the guard exists` and `the guard runs` become indistinguishable to a reader, and this pair spent a year in exactly that state. An exception is a LICENCE, so a precondition nobody reads is not a harmless omission: `architrave-that-is-not-there` was excusing a stucco-over-wood-frame Pueblo Revival house under a licence written for an adobe wall. `construction` is evaluated against the style's RESOLVED kit through build/construction_vocabulary.py, which is a closed table; `date_range` against the style's own period. Where the answer cannot be decided from a style alone the exception is NOT GRANTED and NOT REFUSED -- it is unjudged, and a bounds_test that cannot be resolved makes the whole fault could-not-evaluate rather than silently taking one branch. `regions` is NOT evaluated and is counted: the 45 tokens in use are free text under two spelling conventions and the style corpus's own 219 region names are free text too, so closing it needs a gazetteer ruling and not a mapping.

assets.description: asset ids — the incorrect/correct pair that teaches this

test.description: The measurable form of the fault. Most faults reduce to one ratio against a threshold — leaf width over opening width, pier over opening, garage width over frontage, cornice projection over water-table projection. Putting it here rather than burying it in detection prose makes the corpus executable: a model with measurements from a photograph, or a platform with a model, can evaluate it directly.

direction.description: The condition for CORRECTNESS. The fault is present when it is not met.

measurable_from.description: Whether a model looking at a street photograph can actually evaluate this.

applies_when.description: A precondition on the MEASUREMENTS, as `applies_to_styles` is a precondition on the style. Same shape as a test: expression, direction, threshold. Where it evaluates false the test is NOT RUN -- not passed, not failed, absent from the fault's judgement entirely, exactly as a test scoped to another style is. Where its own measurements are missing the test is could-not-evaluate, because nobody can say whether it applied. This exists because some rules presuppose the thing they measure: `dormer-off-the-bay`'s parity secondary is `dormer_count % 2 == 1`, and on a house STATED to carry no dormers it reported 'Dormers Off the Rhythm: 0 against equals 1'. Zero dormers is not an even number of dormers. Any test whose expression DIVIDES by a count should carry one, or it errors on the house that has none. REQUIRED FIELDS ARE ENFORCED, added 28 Aug 2026 after this package's own adversarial audit found two silent failure modes in a schema-valid guard. Omit `expression` and the precondition is ignored entirely -- the test runs unguarded and convicts, which is the bug the field exists to prevent, wearing the field's name. Omit `direction` and `_eval_test` compares against no operator, `passes` is None, and the test is PERMANENTLY not-applicable: a fault silently switched off for the life of the corpus, reporting `required: "None 1"` to anyone who looks. `between` additionally requires `upper`, or the band collapses to a single value. The failure state of a mistyped guard is a fault going quiet, and this package has just taught every reader that not-applicable is benign.

direction.description: The condition under which the test RUNS.

applies_to_styles.description: Style ids this test is written for. **Absent means every style the fault applies to**, which is the behaviour before this field existed and keeps every fault already in the corpus valid. OQ 63, ruled 24 Aug 2026: `check_measurements` runs every test in `[test] + secondary_tests` and reports the fault present if ANY of them fails, so a secondary test written for one style was failing houses of every other. `chimney-omitted` carries a Tudor Revival chimney-breadth ratio and a Prairie visual-mass test, and both were firing on a Cape Cod colonial -- which is why a parti named `cape-central-chimney` was reported as having no chimney. Matched against the style AND its inheritance chain, so a test scoped to a parent still applies to its descendants.

severity_by_style.description: Severity is not uniform. A missing chimney is fatal on Tudor Revival and Prairie and unremarkable on a ranch; a pork-chop return is fatal on a Georgian and meaningless where there is no cornice.

items.description: Where the OPPOSITE is the fault. A crisp arris is correct almost everywhere and wrong on Cape Dutch, Pueblo and Andalusian, where the fault is the absence of softening.

inverted_by.description: Faults with a polarity: too wide and too narrow, present where absent belongs and absent where present belongs.

co_occurs_with.description: Faults that travel together, usually because they share a driver.

alternative_to.description: Faults that are competing solutions to the same commercial problem and therefore almost never appear together — a raised Cape eave and a wall of dormers are two answers to one question about saleable upper-floor area.

severity_trajectory.description: Where severity changes over time. A cornice gutter with no liner is minor on day one and fatal in year twelve, and the maintenance-driven family all has this shape.

secondary_tests.description: Faults that are genuinely two-part: crown size AND crown projection; porch depth AND deck height above the walk; room depth AND head height; Doric spacing, which needs both a continuous bound and a modular one. In 0.2.0 the second test lived in prose where nothing could execute it.

severity_in_use.description: Severity is defined against the STYLE READING, which is the wrong scale for the plan and services layer. A stack with nowhere to land is invisible in a photograph and fatal in occupation. Two axes, because a corpus that scores only what shows from the street will quietly deprioritise everything that decides whether the house is good to live in.

deprecated_inheritance.description: Where a period practice is correct for its own time and dangerous to inherit. Georgian solar indifference is authentic and should not cascade into a house built today.
